## Keeping your styles

**Your own table styles &middot; Page 2**\
*The page before it is
[1. Making your own style](tables-own-style.qmd).*

Page 1 kept its style in a folder named `styles` inside the project. That suits
a style that belongs to one project, such as one journal's style for one paper,
but the folder goes when the project goes: copy such a style somewhere else
before you delete the project. This page shows where to keep the styles you mean
to keep, so that every project can use them. There's no script to build here:
just a line for a startup file, and a few habits.

## One folder for every project

- **Choose a folder you can see, and that is backed up**, such as a folder
  named `jstats styles` in your Documents folder (or in OneDrive).
- **Set it for every session.** The `style.dir` setting lasts until R
  restarts, so add it to your project's `.Rprofile`, the file
  [Loading jstats automatically](loading-jstats-automatically.qmd) sets up,
  below its `library(jstats)` line:

  ```r
  # Explained on the Keeping your styles page
  joptions(style.dir = "~/jstats styles")
  ```

  An `.Rprofile` belongs to one project, so add the line in each project where
  you make tables. Every project then finds the same styles. jstats creates the
  folder the first time the line runs, if it isn't there.
- **Find the folder.** In R, `~` is usually your Documents folder on Windows
  and your home folder on a Mac. To see exactly where the folder is, run
  `path.expand("~/jstats styles")`.
- **Move a style in.** A style made in a project's own `styles` folder, as on page 1, can be copied into this folder like any file. With the line above in
  place, jstats looks in this folder first, so the copy here is the one it uses.

## Keep copies

A style file is a small text file. Keep a copy of any style you would hate to
lose, and of the version before a big change.

## If no style folder is set

With no style folder set, `jstyle()` with `save.as` saves a copy in your
*jstats folder*, a folder jstats keeps for you, and prints the copy's full
path. That folder is easy to lose track of: it is hidden in File Explorer on
Windows (it sits under AppData) and in Finder on a Mac (under Library).

To open it anyway, copy the full path jstats printed (`jstyle()` with nothing in
the parentheses prints it too, at the end of its list of folders) and paste it
into the address bar of File Explorer on Windows, or into Finder's Go > Go to
Folder on a Mac. To make hidden folders show all the time, search the web for
"show hidden files" and your version of Windows, or for "show Library folder"
on a Mac.

Setting a style folder of your own, as above, keeps your styles where you can see them. Page 3, [Changing a style by hand](tables-by-hand.qmd), changes a
copy of a style.

```{r}
#| label: prose-gates
#| include: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PROSE GATES -- hidden. Each stopifnot() below is one statement the prose
# makes about what the package does; a false one HALTS the render. Every file
# written goes into a temporary folder.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.msgs <- function(expr) {         # what a call prints, both streams, as one string
  m <- character(0)
  o <- withCallingHandlers(utils::capture.output(expr),
                           message = function(c) { m <<- c(m, conditionMessage(c))
                                                   invokeRestart("muffleMessage") })
  paste(c(o, m), collapse = "\n")
}
.td <- tempfile("ks-"); dir.create(.td)
.old_ud <- Sys.getenv("R_USER_DATA_DIR", unset = NA)
Sys.setenv(R_USER_DATA_DIR = file.path(.td, "userdata"))
.jf <- tools::R_user_dir("jstats")
dir.create(.jf, recursive = TRUE)
.np <- function(p) normalizePath(p, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
stopifnot(startsWith(.np(.jf), .np(.td)))   # the temporary one, never the real one
# a path as R hands it over can differ from its normalized form (Windows'
# short names, a linked temporary folder): accept either form in the text
.has_path <- function(text, path) {
  text <- gsub("\\\\", "/", text)
  any(vapply(unique(c(gsub("\\\\", "/", path), .np(path))),
             function(f) grepl(f, text, fixed = TRUE), logical(1)))
}

# joptions() creates a style folder that is not there (a full path here,
# standing in for the .Rprofile line's ~ folder)
.newdir <- file.path(.td, "jstats styles")
.m_new <- .msgs(joptions(style.dir = .newdir))
.made <- dir.exists(.newdir)
# the style folder comes first: a style of the same name in the jstats folder
# is not the one used
invisible(utils::capture.output(jstyle("report", save.as = file.path(.newdir, "same"))))
.alt <- readLines(file.path(.newdir, "same.jstyle"), encoding = "UTF-8")
.alt[which(.alt == "font = Arial")[1]] <- "font = Courier New"
writeLines(.alt, file.path(.jf, "same.jstyle"), useBytes = TRUE)
.font_first <- grep("^font ", utils::capture.output(jstyle("same")), value = TRUE)[1]
# with no style folder set: save.as writes into the jstats folder and prints
# its full path; jstyle() lists the jstats folder last
invisible(utils::capture.output(joptions(style.dir = NULL)))
.m_save <- .msgs(jstyle("report", save.as = "kept"))
.saved <- file.exists(file.path(.jf, "kept.jstyle"))
.lst <- utils::capture.output(jstyle())
.last_folder <- tail(.lst[nzchar(trimws(.lst))], 1)

if (is.na(.old_ud)) Sys.unsetenv("R_USER_DATA_DIR") else Sys.setenv(R_USER_DATA_DIR = .old_ud)
stopifnot(
  grepl("Created the style folder", .m_new, fixed = TRUE), .made,
  grepl("Arial$", .font_first),
  .saved, .has_path(.m_save, .jf),
  grepl("(your jstats folder", .last_folder, fixed = TRUE),
  .has_path(.last_folder, .jf)
)
unlink(.td, recursive = TRUE)
```
